overall: POOR overall: only Coron and Galoc stay GOOD; Maglalambay, Panlaitan and Decabobo slipped to MARGINAL; the east side is shut again with Cabunlawan, Decabaitot, Ciron and Nangalao VERY POOR through Sunday morning
limiterDetail: The main limiter is a combination , led by east wind (Nangalao 19–21 kt all 24h; Cabunlawan/Decabaitot 18.6–23.7 kt, peaking about 8 AM near 23.7; Ciron 19.8–21.8 kt all day; Barangonan 16.7–21.3 kt), plus current at Decabaitot (1.3–1.9 kt about 10 AM–4 PM and again about 10 PM–3 AM Sunday), Alava (1.2–1.6 kt evenings), Barangonan (1.0–1.7 kt evenings), and Tara/Turda (about 1.0–1.2 kt afternoon/evening). Rain is light/minor: 0.1–0.2 mm/h early morning at Nangalao and Barangonan; Linapacan, Cabunlawan and Decabaitot about 9–11 AM. Dry overall.

pagasa.detail: PAGASA: CLEAR. No gale, wind signal or heavy-rain warning for Calamian / MIMAROPA. The feed still lists an older tropical cyclone alert for Typhoon Rosal (Champi) that doesn't name Palawan; worth a glance on the PAGASA site.

changed.title: ⚠️ What changed since yesterday afternoon
items: The fishing mix worsened to 2 GOOD / 7 MARGINAL / 3 POOR / 4 VERY POOR (was 5 GOOD / 4 MARGINAL / 6 POOR / 1 VERY POOR). Maglalambay, Panlaitan and Decabobo dropped out of GOOD into MARGINAL as wind rose to about 10–13 kt. Cabunlawan, Decabaitot and Ciron fell back into VERY POOR as the east wind rebuilt to 20–24 kt (Ciron about 20–22 kt all day). Tara and Turda slipped back to POOR on about 1.0 kt current. Barangonan stays POOR at 17–21 kt. Alava and Linapacan improved POOR→MARGINAL. Only Coron and Galoc remain GOOD.

Saturday regional wind also worsened — now 13 kt, gusts 19 (was 11 g18). Wednesday is 13 kt g17 (was 9.7) and Thursday is the week's worst at 14 kt g19 (was 12). Sunday is still the calmest day (8.3 kt, gusts 14). Sat 7 stays SLIGHTLY SOFT; Sun 8 SLIGHTLY SOFT leaning softer; Mon 9 now NEAR NORMAL (was NORMAL) as the first recovery day after a worse Saturday catch. Tightening risk remains high. Shortage detector ELEVATED Sat–Fri; surge OFF. PAGASA still shows no warning for Palawan.

shortageRisk: Surge flag OFF (unchanged). The dashboard's shortage detector stays ELEVATED for Sat–Fri (guide only; it reacts to the 0.5–0.7 kt daily currents). Tightening risk remains high: soft stretch through Sun 8 arrivals; Mon 9 is the first recovery day. Lean on Coron and Galoc (and Decabobo's afternoon lull about 2–5 PM when wind is 2–5 kt) for weekend supply. Maglalambay and Panlaitan are no longer fully GOOD.

bestWindow.headline: About 2–5 PM at Decabobo; Coron/Galoc workable all day; Maglalambay/Panlaitan overnight Sunday 2–5 AM
details: Decabobo: about 2–5 PM Saturday when wind drops to about 2–5 kt, current 0.2–0.5 (dashboard best hour ~Sat 16). Coron and Galoc: workable all day at 8–13 kt; lightest overnight Sunday about 1–5 AM (5–7 kt), current 0.1–0.4. Tara and Turda: wind is light about 3–5 PM (2–5 kt) but current is 1.0–1.2 then — better about 11 PM–2 AM when current eases to 0.3–0.5. Maglalambay and Panlaitan: easing overnight Sunday about 2–5 AM (5–9 kt, current ≤0.3). East side: no usable window next 24h.
Keep small boats off Nangalao, Cabunlawan, Decabaitot, Ciron and Barangonan today and overnight (up to 24 kt, gusts near 29).
